integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, a fixed 50mm prime close-up frames a young woman with long black straight hair, a pinhead-sized mole 8 mm from the inner corner of her left eye, natural cool-white skin with a makeup-free look, wearing a Japanese sailor-style winter uniform with a striped collar and a thick white scarf wrapped around her neck. Cold winter sunlight wraps her face from the upper left as low-angle side backlight with a high color temperature; low saturation, slight overexposure, fine film grain and a bluish tone give a realistic texture, while the snowy outdoor background dissolves into seamless defocused bokeh with blurred, slowly moving human silhouettes and light spots. The camera holds a completely static shot with zero displacement and zero focal-length change; every emotional beat is carried by micro-expressions limited to 2 mm of facial displacement, unfolding with ultra-slow, 24fps-smooth continuity, no abrupt jumps, no head shaking and no large body movement. She begins with her gaze lowered onto the center of her scarf, lower eyelids fully relaxed and pupils drifting slightly inward; over the first two seconds she lifts her eyes toward the person standing off-screen to the left, and a dewy six-tooth smile rises gradually, completing its ascent smoothly with no sudden burst. Holding the smile with slightly narrowed eyes, she then lets the arc freeze and drain away, leaving only a 1 mm remnant curve at the mouth corners as the expression glides into quiet grievance. A thin flush of red suddenly floods the area near her tear ducts without spreading into the whites of the eyes, and a red film rises across the upper eyelids. The thin redness beneath the lower eyelids then spreads at a visible speed, her pupils dilate almost imperceptibly, and the mouth corners first lift 1 mm and then sink 2 mm as if forcing back a cry; her whole body freezes for half a second while the tear film brims at the lower eyelid yet does not fall. Her gaze drifts slowly from the left and tilts slightly upward to meet the face of the person off-screen; her brows knit with the faintest tremble of sadness rather than anger or confusion, the lower-eyelid redness deepens, and tears well and swirl in her eyes while being fiercely held back. The corners of her eyes and the bridge and wings of her nose flush in the careful control of tears; her mouth corners keep a faint, now-distorted trace of a smile, her chin trembles almost invisibly, her lips part as if to speak yet stop, and faint creases appear on her forehead as she resists the emotional breaking point. Toward the end, a single tear hangs on the verge of falling while she still holds it back, her face suspended between a fading smile and restrained sorrow — to a bystander she would seem calm, and only the person facing her can sense the hidden grief, her emotional curve traveling from hidden joy to sudden grievance, solitary heaviness, a soft release, and finally reluctant attachment.

widgets_values:
# LTX-2.5

LTX-2.5 is Lightricks' open video generation model : fast, local-first, and built for production. Run it locally, fine-tune it for your own use case, or integrate it into your pipeline.

**Key highlights:**

- **Pixel Diffusion** : keyframes-first generation that builds every scene on a grid of high-fidelity keyframes for industry-leading pixel quality
- **Diffusion Video Decoder** : sharper faces, legible text, fewer smears in fast motion
- **Native multishot** : one generation yields multiple connected shots holding character, environment, lighting, voice, and style across cuts
- **Custom Gemma 4 12B text encoder** : retains multiple subjects, actions, lighting, detail, and camera direction across complex prompts
- **Dedicated Prompt Enhancer** : a lightweight model that expands short prompts into rich cinematic instructions at near-zero extra compute
- **Auto Duration** : predicts the right clip length from the described action before diffusion begins
- **Better distilled model** : carries far more quality, prompt adherence, and motion into a smaller, faster variant
- Carried over from LTX-2.3: native 4K, synchronized audio-video

Official model & files: https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5
## What this workflow does

This **Image-to-Video** workflow animates a first frame into a video. Load a starting image, describe the motion in the prompt, and the model continues the scene while holding character, lighting, and style : with synchronized audio.

## Subgraph parameters

The **Image to Video (LTX-2.5)** node is a subgraph. Click the **Enter subgraph** button at the bottom of the node to open its internal graph, where you can inspect and fine-tune every step of the pipeline (conditioning, sampler, CFG guider, VAE decode, and more).

| Parameter | What it does |
|---|---|
| first_frame | Starting image that the video continues from (load your own image in **Load First Frame**) |
| prompt | Text prompt describing the motion, scene, lighting, camera, and style |
| prompt_enhance | Toggle the built-in Prompt Enhancer: expands short prompts into rich cinematic instructions at near-zero extra compute |
| duration | Clip length in seconds (Auto Duration can predict it from the action) |
| width / height | Output resolution in pixels (e.g. 1280×720) |
| seed | Random seed : set a fixed value to reproduce the same result |
| frame_rate | Frames per second |
| unet_name | Main model: LTX-2.5 distilled transformer (ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors) |
| video_vae | Video VAE used for decoding (ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors) |
| audio_vae | Audio VAE that produces synchronized audio (ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors) |
| clip_name | Text encoder: custom Gemma 4 12B with projection (gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors) |
| upscale_model | Latent upscaler applied before decoding for higher-fidelity output |
| prompt_enhance_model | Model checkpoint used by the Prompt Enhancer |

## How to use

1. Download the models listed in **Note: Model Links** and place them in ComfyUI's `models/` folder
2. Replace the image in **Load First Frame** with your own starting frame
3. Write a prompt describing the motion, optionally toggle **prompt_enhance** for short prompts
4. Set **duration** / **width** / **height** / **frame_rate** (defaults work well) and hit **Queue**
5. To dive deeper, click **Enter subgraph** at the bottom of the main node : every internal step (conditioning, sampler, CFG, VAE decode) can be edited there

## Report Issue

Note: Please update ComfyUI first ([guide](https://docs.comfy.org/installation/update_comfyui)) and prepare required models. Desktop/Cloud updates follow stable releases, so some nightly-supported models may not be available yet.

- Cannot run / runtime errors: [ComfyUI/issues](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/issues)
- UI / frontend issues: [ComfyUI_frontend/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/issues)
- Workflow issues: [workflow_templates/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/issues)
